experiment: E5b — adjudication of flags on the golden (in-session) extraction
adjudicator: claude-opus-5, reading native-resolution entry crops against the extractor's recorded value and stated doubt
sample: 18 flags drawn round-robin across flagged fields from the four 1910 quarters (seed 7); 16 rendered, 14 adjudicable

taxonomy.error: transcription is wrong — the flag caught a real mistake
taxonomy.degraded: transcription is right (or the best available reading); the source really is hard to read
taxonomy.artifact: transcription is right; the CATALOG is irregular here — a collision, an omission, a printer's error
taxonomy.plausibility: transcription is right and the source is perfectly legible; the flag reports an unusual value, not a doubtful reading
taxonomy.not_adjudicable: the rendered crop does not show the field in question

verdicts.note: reg 249 is clearly printed; it genuinely collides with p28 s12. A catalog fact, not a misreading.
187 is crisply printed. Flag reports an atypical (non-round) print run, not a doubtful digit.
the page really does print 'intique'. Transcription faithful; the Reporter's compositor erred.
page prints 'Stara-i-Hiud Press' (broken n). Flag records it, but the stored value was silently normalised to 'Stara-i-Hind' — a small verbatim-layer deviation worth noting.
column 6 falls outside the rendered crop.
page reads 'Magazine P r e s s,' with a trailing comma and no city. Empty value is correct.
'Marik Singh, B.' is clearly printed. If it is a misprint for Malik, it is the catalog's.
page prints '1318 Hijri' against a June 1910 Christian date; 1328 would be correct. Source error, faithfully transcribed.
pagination genuinely smudged; 108 is a reasonable reading, 168 not excluded. A real 'check my reading' case.
page reads 'litho., edition.' with no ordinal. Empty value is correct.
last word smudged; reading resolved from the gloss ('wearing of chaplets'), which supports Sihra. Correct, and correctly reasoned.
no price line printed before the next section header. Empty value is correct.
1037 clearly printed; collides with a Q3 entry. Catalog fact.
column 6 falls outside the rendered crop.
serial genuinely obscured by the earlier hand's pencil X; 6 inferred from the run. Plausible, not directly verifiable.
second draw (seed 11), after the crop was widened to column 6. Leading digit of '1,000' is cut at the column rule; reading is right but not directly verifiable.
second draw. Column 6 now visible and the flag is exactly right: 'No. 1__ dated the 6__ September, 191_' is cut at the right page edge.
second draw. Margin serial overwritten by the earlier hand's pencil; 100 inferred from the run.

second_draw_note: Items 17-19 come from a separate stratified draw (seed 11) made to verify the widened crop. They are pooled with the first draw in the totals; both are random draws over the same population, but the pooling is stated because it was not planned in advance.
